channelTitle: Grandma June's nightcap tea isn't chamomile, and it's stronger than you'd think
hook: Before chamomile got popular, this earthy root tea was Grandma June's actual bedtime secret.
remedy: Valerian root steeped into a strong, earthy tea has been an old-fashioned bedtime staple for generations, long used to help an overactive mind settle down before sleep. Its strong smell put some households off, but the ones who swore by it always kept a jar on hand.
steps: Steep one teaspoon of dried valerian root in a cup of hot water for ten to fifteen minutes, covered
Strain out the root, and stir in a little honey if the earthy taste is too strong
Drink it warm about thirty minutes before bed, not right when you're already lying down
caution: Valerian root can make you drowsy, so don't drive or operate machinery after drinking it. Skip it if you're pregnant, nursing, or already taking sleep medication or sedatives, and check with a doctor if you take other prescriptions.
cta: Does your family have a go-to bedtime tea, or did valerian root ever make an appearance in your house? Tell Grandma June.
